title: Model-output JSON schema and safety/decision-caution label definitions
description: The six-field JSON output contract stated in the experimental prompts. This schema documents the historical requirements; it is not a claim that all requirements were implemented by the runtime validator or satisfied by all saved outputs.

current_state_interpretation.description: Concise interpretation of current state, at most two sentences.

risk_identification.description: Risk or concern; when no clear risk: 'No clear acute risk identified from available inputs.' Not the string 'null'.

training_adjustment_suggestion.description: Concrete Day t+1 training/activity adjustment, at most three sentences.

supporting_evidence.description: Two to five evidence objects; exact input-variable names.

claim.description: Claim supported by the selected variable.

safety_flag.description: Model-produced safety flag: none, caution, or stop.

x-label-definitions.none: No clear concern from available inputs.
x-label-definitions.caution: Poor sleep, elevated fatigue/stress/soreness, reduced readiness, unusually high load, or adverse recent trend suggests modification.
x-label-definitions.stop: Severe or multiple concerning signals suggest avoiding hard training and seeking human coach/medical review; requires strong directly grounded evidence.

caveats.description: Missing or intentionally withheld information when relevant.

$comment: Machine-readable documentation assembled from the historical prompt text and validation/analysis code on 2026-09-28. It is not a pre-existing schema artifact or a preregistration record. The derived decision-caution label is documented under $defs and x-derived-label and is not a seventh model-generated field. Sentence limits, exact input-variable visibility and semantic appropriateness require separate checks.

decision_caution_label.description: Derived analysis label named decision_bucket in the analysis code; obtained by lexical rules applied after generation, not emitted as an additional field by the model.

x-derived-label.input: The space-separated concatenation of risk_identification, training_adjustment_suggestion, and complete raw_text, converted to lowercase. If the parsed payload is absent, the first two strings are empty; raw_text is still scanned.
x-derived-label.matching: Python regular-expression search; first match wins in ascending priority order; unclear is the fallback. Word boundaries are applied as written. The rules do not generally resolve negation.

categories.label: stop_or_medical_caution
categories.definition: Stop-training or medical-caution wording matched by the first rule.

categories.label: reduce_or_recovery
categories.definition: Reduced-load, rest, or recovery wording, when the preceding rule does not match.

categories.label: increase_or_progress
categories.definition: Increased-load or progression wording, when neither preceding rule matches.

categories.label: maintain
categories.definition: Maintain-current-training wording, when no higher-priority rule matches.

categories.label: unclear
categories.definition: No match to the preceding four lexical categories.

x-derived-label.historical_version_note: The earlier script 21 rule omits deload from reduce_or_recovery. Script 23 is the version used for the stored robustness/grounding label recheck. Audit lexica are preserved by source in ../07_audit_lexica/audit_lexica_by_source.json.

x-historical-runtime-validation.scope: Applied after parsing a JSON object: exactly the six top-level fields, supporting_evidence is an array, and safety_flag is none, caution or stop. The five batch validators implement the same acceptance conditions.
x-historical-runtime-validation.omitted_checks: The historical validator did not enforce string types for the other top-level fields, evidence-item fields/types, evidence count, direction categories, sentence limits, or semantic grounding.
x-historical-runtime-validation.interpretation: Runtime acceptance does not imply full prompt-contract compliance. Saved outputs are retained without correction. The structural check does not independently adjudicate sentence counts or semantic appropriateness.

x-documentation-sources: Historical prompt JSON instructions and safety-flag rules
Identical validate_payload functions in the five generation-batch scripts
